strategy_title: Autotune Large XBLOCK Causes Register Spill and Instruction Explosion
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with large XBLOCK configs (512, 1024, 2048) to a pointwise kernel caused registers per thread to jump from 18 to 48, reducing Block Limit Registers from 21 to 5 and theoretical occupancy from 100% to 62.5%. More critically, executed instructions exploded from ~1.3M to ~8.4M (6.5x increase), indicating the autotuner selected a config that dramatically increased per-thread work or caused register spilling, resulting in 2.86x longer kernel duration despite improved scheduler utilization. When a kernel already has low register pressure (≤20 registers/thread) and the autotune decorator itself causes register count to balloon, the occupancy loss and instruction overhead far outweigh any partial-wave tail benefit.
slow_pseudocode:
# Before: fixed XBLOCK=128, 18 regs/thread, 3675 blocks, 1.74 waves/SM
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_out_ptr0, in_ptr0, ..., xnumel, XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    xindex = tl.program_id(0) * XBLOCK + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)[:]
    # pointwise BN + hardtanh
    ...
grid = (cdiv(470400, 128),)  # 3675 blocks
kernel[grid](..., XBLOCK=128)
applicable_when: Never: this specific pattern (autotune with large XBLOCK on a kernel with originally low register count) caused severe regression. Do not apply when the kernel has ≤20 registers/thread and adding autotune causes register count to increase by >2x.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel has low register pressure (≤20 regs/thread) AND adding autotune decorator causes register count to balloon (>2x increase). The LaunchConfiguration NCU rule may flag partial-wave overhead, but if the fix causes register spilling or instruction count explosion, the cure is worse than the disease. Also avoid when the autotune overhead itself (compilation of multiple configs) is not amortized by repeated kernel calls.
framework_notes: In Triton, adding @triton.autotune can cause the compiler to allocate more registers per thread when larger XBLOCK values are explored, because the compiler must handle the worst-case tile size. This can reduce Block Limit Registers from the register file perspective, capping theoretical occupancy well below 100%. The instruction count explosion (6.5x here) suggests the selected config may have introduced loop unrolling or other compiler artifacts that multiplied work. Always verify register count after adding autotune.
